title: Temperature-series changes offset 49% of the SST radiation contribution in a symmetric fit decomposition for nine model pairs in 1981-2010
abstract: We separated changes in radiation and in the temperature predictor in nine published model pairs with identical sea ice and external forcing but different SST data. For 1981-2010, the mean AMIP-minus-HadISST1 radiation-on-temperature slope gap is -0.243 W m-2 K-1. An exact symmetric two-input decomposition gives a radiation contribution of -0.474 and a temperature-series contribution of +0.231. The latter offsets 49% of the former in this sample. Both orders retain a larger negative radiation contribution than the total gap. The temperature contribution is positive in seven pairs. It includes covariance changes as well as variance changes. Removing 1982 retains a 44% offset. Clear-sky longwave and shortwave cloud radiative effect supply the largest negative radiation contributions. However, all tested year-block intervals for the temperature contribution include zero. Radiation intervals also include zero at block lengths five and seven. These results audit the fitted estimand; they do not identify SST error, prove a splice effect or calibrate Green's functions. Code, source hashes, aggregate fit estimates and all resampling estimates are supplied. No new model runs or observations are used.
